requirements_summary: Latency-sensitive product reranking and personalization at checkout. Target: p95 <= 80-120ms for 64-128 token responses; peak throughput ~800-1,200 qps during promotions. Cost-sensitive: minimize per-request per-token cost; prefer batching and prefix/KV caching for repeated context (user profile + session). Interested in aggressive quantization (4-bit/INT8) if quality drop negligible. Need deterministic fallbacks: fallback to smaller model variant when latency SLO at risk. Routing by region and cost tier required (US primary, EU data residency).
notes:
- CTO Elena Park: 'if we can keep p95 under 100ms during Black Friday spikes and show predictable billing, we'll go enterprise.'
- Current infra: hybrid (AWS + GCP), uses Redis for session state; inference today is mostly in-house TF endpoints (high cost, inconsistent latency).
- POC focus: measure p95 and token cost for three configurations: hosted fp16, dedicated fp16 w/ batching, dedicated 4-bit quantized w/ caching.
- SE recommendation: run constant-load throughput tests and tail-latency tracking, instrument KV cache hit rates. Also include jitter under autoscaling bursts.
- Security: require SSO/SAML and KMS with customer-managed keys for production; retention controls for logs for 12 months.
- Quote from Head of ML Ops: 'We can trade 5-7% quality for 40% cost savings if ranking delta within threshold.'
poa: 1) SE to run 48h dedicated cluster test (quantized + batching) by 2026-03-10. 2) Deliver cost model comparing 1M token scenarios and embedding cache hit impacts. 3) Security to validate KMS flow and produce integration plan. 4) Commercial to propose ELA with burst credits for promotional windows.
recent_bench_findings: Initial run: p95=140ms fp16 (no batching) for 512-token sessions; enabling 8-request batching reduced p95 to 90ms but increased median latency; 4-bit quantized build reduced infra cost estimate by ~38% in model execution but introduced 2-3% delta on reranking score in A/B sample. Cache warm-up showed 58% KV hit rate for repeated product-context prefixes in 10k session sample.
